newsitem.title: UK: Cook wants UK on par with France, Germany.
newsitem.headline: Cook wants UK on par with France, Germany.

text.p: New Foreign Secretary Robin Cook on Monday risked offending Italy for the second time in a week by reaffirming that Britain wanted to rank alongside France and Germany in playing a leading role in Europe.
Officials in Rome rebuked Cook last week when he failed to mention Italy in the same breath as France, Germany and Britain.

They pointed out that in terms of voting strength within the European Union the four countries were equal. "There are four major countries and all of them are in a position of absolute parity," one Italian diplomat said.
Asked on Monday about the row, Cook said he made no apology for wanting to make Britain a leading player in Europe.
"We wish Britain to be of equal status with either France or Germany," he told a news conference at which he set out the Labour government's foreign policy priorities.
"We are working to make sure that we shape the agenda and not react to the agenda shaped by others," he added.

But Cook went some way to mend fences, saying he was keen to visit Rome to work out with Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini a common approach to next month's EU summit in Amsterdam, which will overhaul the workings of the 15-nation bloc.
"Italy is indeed a very important member of the European Union," Cook said.

Italy is sensitive to the way it is perceived within the EU because of speculation that Germany might try to exclude it from the first wave of countries due to launch a single European currency in 1999.
